claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you find out if you're eligible for Child Benefit.

To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you a few questions about your circumstances.

Let's start with the basics:

**Do you currently live in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for confirming that you live in the UK.

**How many children would you like to claim Child Benefit for, and what are their names and ages?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I have one child - Alex, who is 17 years old.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information about Alex.

Since Alex is 17 years old (over 16), eligibility for Child Benefit depends on their current situation.

**Is Alex currently in any of the following?**
- Full-time approved education (such as A-levels, Scottish Highers, NVQs up to Level 3, or similar qualifications)
- An approved training course (not an apprenticeship)
- Neither of the above

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex isn't in education or training at the moment. They finished school but haven't started anything else yet.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying. Since Alex is 17 and has recently left education or training, there may still be a way to qualify for Child Benefit.

**Has Alex registered with any of the following since leaving education?**
- A government-sponsored careers service (such as the National Careers Service in England, Careers Wales, Skills Development Scotland, or similar)
- The armed services

If Alex has registered with one of these within the last 20 weeks, you may still be able to claim Child Benefit for a limited period.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex hasn't registered with any careers service or the armed forces.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information.

I have a couple more questions to ensure I fully understand the situation:

**Is Alex currently doing any of the following?**
- Working 24 hours or more per week in paid employment
- On an apprenticeship in England
- Receiving benefits in their own right (such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex isn't working that much - just does a bit here and there. They're not on an apprenticeship and don't get any benefits in their own name.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that.

Just one more question to confirm your living situation:

**Does Alex live with you, or do you contribute financially towards their upkeep (for example, towards food, clothes, or pocket money)?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, Alex lives at home with me.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Based on the information you've provided, I'm afraid **you are not currently eligible for Child Benefit for Alex**.

Here's why:

**For Alex (age 17):**
- You meet the basic requirements: you live in the UK and Alex lives with you.
- However, for children aged 16 or over, Child Benefit can normally only continue if the child remains in **approved education or training**.
- Since Alex has left education and is not currently in approved education or training, this key requirement is not met.
- There is an option to continue receiving Child Benefit for up to **20 weeks** if a 16 or 17 year old registers with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed services after leaving education — but Alex has not done this.

**What you could do:**
If Alex registers with a government-sponsored careers service (such as the National Careers Service in England), you may be able to apply for Child Benefit to continue for up to 20 weeks. Alternatively, if Alex returns to approved education or training before they turn 20, you could become eligible again at that point.

I hope this helps clarify your situation. If you have any other questions, please feel free to ask.

Since none of these conditions are met, the claimant is not eligible for Child Benefit for Alex.
